reading: Each isolated marker cell becomes the centre of a 3x3 stamp (2 in the centre, 1 orthogonally, 3 diagonally), and full row and column lines of 1 are drawn through every stamp centre to the grid border.
why: every input marker is the centre of an identical 3x3 unit [313/121/313]; from each centre, lines of colour 1 run in all four directions to the border
invariants: background cells off the lines and stamps

reading: Each 8-connected group of 4s is part of a plus shape (centre + 4 arms); the plus that contains the whole group and has no 0 cell is completed by turning its 5 cells into 2.

new_rows.name: plus_gap
new_rows.datalog:
pl(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
pl(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
pc(Y, X, Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
pc(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- px(Y, X, C), pl(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C2).
touch4(Y, X, O) :- pc(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 4), obj(O, Y2, X2).
spill(Y, X) :- touch4(Y, X, O), obj(O, Y3, X3), !pc(Y, X, Y3, X3).
holed(Y, X) :- touch4(Y, X, O), pc(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 0).
good(Y, X) :- touch4(Y, X, O), !spill(Y, X), !holed(Y, X).
plus_gap(Y2, X2) :- good(Y, X), pc(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 5).

why: every changed cell is a 5 inside a plus whose 4-cells form whole 4-components and which has no 0; 5 -> 2 there, nothing else changes

reading: Every object that is exactly the outline of a square box (side >= 2, solid 2x2 included) gets eight 2-cells placed just outside its four corners, one above/below and one left/right of each corner cell.

gap(O) :- box(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), px(Y, X, C), X = X0, Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, !obj(O, Y, X).
gap(O) :- box(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), px(Y, X, C), X = X1, Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, !obj(O, Y, X).

corner_out(Y, X) :- sqf(O), box(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y1 + 1, X = X1, px(Y, X, C).
corner_out(Y, X) :- sqf(O), box(O, Y0, Y1, X0, X1), Y = Y1, X = X1 + 1, px(Y, X, C).

why: the only changes are background cells set to 2 at the 8 orthogonal outside-corner positions of each square-outline object; non-square shapes (lines, rectangles, diagonal pairs) get nothing

reading: The grey (5) shape is exactly partitioned into 2x2 squares and 1x3 straight bars; squares are coloured 8 and bars are coloured 2.

slots.pieces: 2x2 square (colour 8) and 1x3 bar in either orientation (colour 2)
slots.rule: find the exact cover of the shape by these pieces and paint each piece its colour

why: every 5 cell becomes 8 or 2; the 8 cells group into 2x2 blocks and the 2 cells into straight 3-cell bars, covering the shape exactly

reading: A corner key area (6x6, i.e. a 3x3 mask drawn in 2x2 blocks of a key colour) shows a pattern; in every 3x3 panel of 0/1 cells (panels separated by 4-lines) whose 1s cover all mask positions, those mask cells are recoloured to the key colour.

slots.key: the 6x6 corner block downscaled 2x to a 3x3 mask of the key colour
slots.panels: 3x3 cells between the colour-4 separator lines
slots.condition: panel has 1 at every mask position
slots.action: mask cells in that panel 1 -> key colour

why: only 1 cells change, only to the key colour, only in panels where the whole key mask is present as 1s, and exactly at the mask positions
invariants: panels that do not contain the mask

reading: Each closed rectilinear loop has its corners recoloured: convex corners (diagonal cell between the two arms is inside the loop) become 4, concave corners (that diagonal cell is outside) become 2.

out(Y2, X2) :- out(Y, X), ortho(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgc(Y2, X2).

reading: The 3x3 input has one all-one-colour row or column; the 9x9 output places three copies of the input along that block row or block column and leaves the rest 0.
why: output is 3x3 blocks of the input size; block (i,j) is a copy of the input iff row i (or column j) of the input is the uniform line, else empty

reading: Top and bottom rows are full lines of two colours; every object moves straight up or down toward the line of its own colour until it touches that line, keeping its shape.
why: each single-colour object keeps its shape and column, ending adjacent to the border line of its colour; note pair 0 has two extra 8 cells at (10,15),(11,15) that no shape-keeping move explains (likely task noise)

reading: In every column whose bottom cell is coloured (5), each coloured cell draws its colour upward until the next coloured cell above it; the topmost one extends to the top border. Other columns are unchanged.

reading: The grid is three 3x3 panels side by side, each holding a 5-pattern; each panel is filled entirely with the colour its pattern stands for (top row->6, hollow square->3, bottom row->1, anti-diagonal->9, centre dot->4).

slots.action: fill whole panel with the looked-up colour

why: each output panel is uniform and its colour is a fixed function of the input panel's 5-pattern, consistent across all pairs
